newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares cheer March CPI drop to 6.0pct.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares cheer March CPI drop to 6.0pct.

text.p: Share prices at the Athens stock exchange gained 1.95 percent on Friday, moved by a better-than-expected drop in March CPI-inflation, which fell to 6.0 percent year-on-year, brokers said.
Market watchers said the inflation drop to 6.0 percent from 6.6 percent in February was a further confirmation of its long-term downward trend amidst other positive corporate developments.
"The inflation drop raises hopes of further interest rate cuts, especially in view of further easing in April due to lower fuel prices," said analyst Vassilis Kletsas at Telesis Securities.
The finalisation of OTE's second flotation announced by the government on Friday was viewed by market participants as another booster of market sentiment.

Greece will sell another 10.7 percent of OTE telecom in June followed by a 7.5 percent rights issue 15 days later. If demand proves strong it may up the float by an additional 2.0 percent, national economy minister Yannos Papandoniou said.
"Market conditions for OTE's upcoming part-flotation and share capital increase are quite favourable." he said.
"The market is clearly focused on large caps and this may continue for a while before buying interest starts looking at medium capitalisation shares." Kletsas added.

The Athens general share index finished 1.95 percent or 26.63 points higher at 1,395.69 from Thursday's 1,369.06 close. Despite a lazy start, turnover picked up at mid-session to reach 15.4 billion drachmas on volume of 4.4 million shares.
Advancers led decliners 162 to 57 with 28 issues unchanged on 247 traded.
Banks, industrials and construction stocks gained about 2.5 percent, with other sectors also ending a touch firmer.
Erlikon, Viohalko and Etem of the Stassinopoulos Group of metallurgical companies hit the upper volatility limit of 8.0 percent.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted higher at 1,029.00-1067.00. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, closed up 50 drachmas at 6,100.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $59.04-$60.73. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The recently issued ING Baring Financial Products American- style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted higher at 2,102-2,294 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
